sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形节目对美国宪法的深度拆解。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm Elizabeth Jo.
sentences.zh: 我是伊丽莎白·乔。

sentences.en: Today, we're discussing Articles 6 and 7.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来讨论第六条和第七条。

sentences.en: Roman, why don't we go through both articles and let's save the most important part for laSt.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，我们为什么不把这两条都过一遍，然后把最重要的部分留到最后呢？

sentences.en: Okay, because there's a lot of unimportant parts.
sentences.zh: 行，因为有很多不太重要的部分。

sentences.en: Less important.
sentences.zh: 相对没那么重要。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: So why don't we start with Article 7?
sentences.zh: 那我们先从第七条开始怎么样？

sentences.en: That's the ratification clause.
sentences.zh: 那是批准条款。

sentences.en: It may be the least important to talk about today, but actually crucially important for the Constitution itself.
sentences.zh: 它可能是今天讨论中最不重要的一条，但实际上对宪法本身至关重要。

sentences.en: We needed these states to vote on it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要这些州对它进行投票。

sentences.en: And the ratification clause says that nine states would be enough to ratify or make the Constitution itself a legitimate document.
sentences.zh: 而批准条款规定，九个州就足以批准或使宪法本身成为一份合法文件。

sentences.en: So that, in fact, happened.
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上确实如此。

sentences.en: It comes into effect on June 21st, 1788, when New Hampshire became the ninth state of the 13 to ratify the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 它于1788年6月21日生效，当时新罕布什尔州成为了批准宪法的第13个州中的第9个州。

sentences.en: So it kind of has its own clause to make sure the document is legit.
sentences.zh: 所以它有点像自带一个条款，用来确保这份文件是合法的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 对，所以这挺清晰的。

sentences.en: There are no real important Supreme Court cases on it.
sentences.zh: 关于它并没有什么真正重要的最高法院判例。

sentences.en: So let's turn back to Article 6.
sentences.zh: 那我们转回第六条。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Article 6 is a mishmash of a bunch of different things.
sentences.zh: 第六条是一堆不同事情的大杂烩。

sentences.en: So Article 6, Clause 1 talks about debts that the United States is already obligated for and still has to pay.
sentences.zh: 第六条第一款讨论的是美国已经承担且仍须偿还的债务。

sentences.en: And so why is that there?
sentences.zh: 那为什么会有这个呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know, when the Constitution was drafted, the country still had debts and engagements that were left over from the Revolutionary War.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，当宪法起草时，国家依然背负着独立战争留下的债务和契约。

sentences.en: And creditors were kind of nervous.
sentences.zh: 债权人们有点紧张。

sentences.en: What if you create a Constitution that wipes out all of the debt?
sentences.zh: 要是你们搞出一部宪法把所有债务一笔勾销了怎么办？

sentences.en: That would be pretty convenient.
sentences.zh: 那可就太方便了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 懂了。

sentences.en: So in order to assuage those nervous creditors, this Constitution, our Constitution, actually says, don't worry,
sentences.zh: 所以为了安抚那些紧张的债权人，这部宪法，也就是我们的宪法，其实在说：别担心，

sentences.en: we understand that we have these debts and we are going to pay these debts.
sentences.zh: 我们理解我们有这些债务，而且我们会偿还这些债务。

sentences.en: So today it's really mostly historical intereSt.
sentences.zh: 所以今天它基本上只具有历史兴趣了。

sentences.en: It doesn't come up because we did, in fact, pay our debts.
sentences.zh: 它不会被提及，因为我们事实上确实还清了债务。

sentences.en: I will say what is interesting is that from Clause 1, originally as it was drafted,
sentences.zh: 我得说，有趣的是，根据最初起草的第一款，

sentences.en: the clause said that the United States would both be obligated to pay the debts and would have the power to pay the debts.
sentences.zh: 该条款规定美国既有义务偿还债务，也有权力偿还债务。

sentences.en: But that second part got taken out of Article 6 and put into Article 1 as part of Congress's spending authority.
sentences.zh: 但第二部分从第六条中被拿了出来，放到了第一条里，作为国会支出权力的一部分。

sentences.en: So that very, very important part today is actually in the larger chunk of the Constitution we cite all the time, which is why does Congress have the ability to pass laws?
sentences.zh: 所以今天这个非常非常重要的部分，实际上在我们经常引用的那部分更大的宪法里，这也是为什么国会有能力通过法律？

sentences.en: And very often it's because of spending authority.
sentences.zh: 而且往往是因为支出权力。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Well, that's really fascinating, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实真的挺迷人的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, you know, one little switch around made a big difference.
sentences.zh: 所以，你看，一个小小的改动就带来了巨大的差异。

sentences.en: Yeah, made a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 对，带来了巨大的差异。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's the first clause.
sentences.zh: 这就是第一款。

sentences.en: Okay, let's turn to Clause 3 of Article 6.
sentences.zh: 好，我们来看看第六条第三款。

sentences.en: Do you want to read it?
sentences.zh: 你想读一下吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The senators and representatives before mentioned and the members of the several state legislatures and all executive and judicial officers,
sentences.zh: 上述参议员和众议员以及各州议会成员，以及美国和各州的所有行政和司法官员，

sentences.en: both of the United States and of the several states, shall be bound by oath or affirmation to support this Constitution.
sentences.zh: 均应宣誓或郑重声明拥护本宪法。

sentences.en: But no religious test shall ever be required as a qualification to any office or public trust under the United States.
sentences.zh: 但不得以任何宗教考核作为担任美国任何公职或信托职务的资格要求。

sentences.en: So this is known as the No Religious Test Clause.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的无宗教考核条款。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I like this clause.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个条款。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: It's kind of, you know, no religious test for anybody taking office.
sentences.zh: 这有点像，你知道的，任何人担任公职都没有宗教考核。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's the absence of religious tests that makes us understand that this is successful, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是由于宗教考核的缺失，才让我们明白这是成功的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We don't require anybody to take a religious teSt.
sentences.zh: 我们不要求任何人接受宗教考核。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But sort of, at least formally, right?
sentences.zh: 但某种程度上，至少在形式上是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there's no formal test, but you can kind of feel it in there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有形式上的考核，但你能在其中隐约感觉得到。

sentences.en: The fact that the representation of other religious faiths is not super common inside of our public institutions.
sentences.zh: 其他宗教信仰的代表在我们的公共机构内部并不是超级常见这一事实。

sentences.en: True, true.
sentences.zh: 确实，确实。

sentences.en: But there is a big difference when you are formally required to do it.
sentences.zh: 但当你被形式上要求这么做时，那就有很大区别了。

sentences.en: And in fact, this clause comes from traditions going back to England.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个条款源于可以追溯到英格兰的传统。

sentences.en: So, for instance, in England in the 17th century, for example, all government officials had to take an oath that they would help establish the Church of England.
sentences.zh: 比如，在17世纪的英格兰，所有政府官员都必须宣誓，宣誓他们将协助建立英格兰教会。

sentences.en: And also disclaim Catholicism and the Pope.
sentences.zh: 并且还要排斥天主教和教皇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so the idea is we have this common law tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的想法是，我们拥有这种普通法传统。

sentences.en: It comes from England.
sentences.zh: 它源自英格兰。

sentences.en: By the time you have the colonies and the Articles of Confederation,
sentences.zh: 到了殖民地和《邦联条例》时期，

sentences.en: it was pretty common for governor officials to be told that they had to take some kind of religious affirmation.
sentences.zh: 政府官员被要求进行某种宗教宣誓是相当普遍的。

sentences.en: Of course, not for the Church of England, but some kind of I believe in God sort of teSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，不是为了英格兰教会，而是某种“我信仰上帝”之类的考核。

sentences.en: It's notable that it's absent.
sentences.zh: 它的缺席是值得注意的。

sentences.en: It's notable for its absence.
sentences.zh: 它因其缺席而引人注目。

sentences.en: And this clause as well has very little in terms of Supreme Court interest or case law today.
sentences.zh: 而且这个条款在今天的最高法院兴趣或判例法方面也非常少。

sentences.en: And that's for a totally different reason.
sentences.zh: 这是出于完全不同的原因。

sentences.en: You'll notice this is about, you know, religious freedom essentially, right?
sentences.zh: 你会注意到这基本上是关于宗教自由的，对吧？

sentences.en: It shouldn't matter whether you are a practicing Catholic or Muslim or Jew to be able to take a public office.
sentences.zh: 你是否能担任公职，不应该取决于你是一个笃信天主教、穆斯林还是犹太人。

sentences.en: But the reason why this clause doesn't get much attention is that's because free exercise clause cases today come up under the First Amendment, right, rather than this clause.
sentences.zh: 但这个条款没有受到太多关注的原因是，如今自由行使条款的案件都是根据第一修正案提出的，而不是根据这个条款。

sentences.en: So not too much there as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这方面也没有太多内容。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I noticed in our recap, you had Article 6, Clause 1 and Article 6, Clause 3, but we have skipped Article 6, Clause 2.
sentences.zh: 所以我注意到在我们的回顾中，你提到了第六条第一款和第六条第三款，但我们跳过了第六条第二款。

sentences.en: So what is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Well, Article 6, Clause 2 contains what's called the Supremacy Clause.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第六条第二款包含了所谓的至高条款。

sentences.en: Why don't you read it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不读一下呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This Constitution and the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance thereof and all treaties made or which shall be made under the authority of the United States shall be the supreme law of the land.
sentences.zh: 本宪法及依本宪法所制定之合众国法律，以及在合众国权力下已经缔结或将要缔结的一切条约，皆为全国之最高法律。

sentences.en: And that's referred to as the Supremacy Clause.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的至高条款。

sentences.en: So why is the Supremacy Clause so important?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么至高条款如此重要呢？

sentences.en: Well, historically, the Supremacy Clause responds to a very particular problem.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，至高条款是对一个非常特定问题的回应。

sentences.en: And that is before the federal constitution, the Articles of Confederation, which was the predecessor document, had no similar provision saying that federal law is supreme.
sentences.zh: 那就是在联邦宪法之前，作为前身文件的《邦联条例》没有类似的规定说明联邦法律是至高无上的。

sentences.en: And you might wonder, well, what does that really mean?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，嗯，这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, think of it this way.
sentences.zh: 好吧，换个角度想。

sentences.en: If you have state laws on a topic and federal laws on the exact same topic, which one are you supposed to follow?
sentences.zh: 如果某个议题既有州法律，又有完全相同的联邦法律，你应该听哪一个？

sentences.en: If there's no clear instruction, well, maybe you just follow whichever one you want.
sentences.zh: 如果没有明确的指示，好吧，也许你想遵循哪个就遵循哪个。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what happened.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是当时发生的情况。

sentences.en: Before the constitution, state courts sometimes just didn't think that federal law was binding, so they didn't apply it.
sentences.zh: 在宪法出台之前，州法院有时只是认为联邦法律不具约束力，所以不予适用。

sentences.en: They applied state law.
sentences.zh: 他们适用的是州法。

sentences.en: That's kind of a problem, right?
sentences.zh: 这算是个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So the Supremacy Clause, just with one fell swoop with this particular clause, gets rid of that uncertainty or ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 所以至高条款，仅仅通过这一个特定条款的一记绝招，就消除了这种不确定性或模糊性。

sentences.en: The Supremacy Clause simply says, look, federal law, whether we mean the constitution, federal statutes, federal treaties, are supreme when it comes to any conflicting state law.
sentences.zh: 至高条款简单地说就是：看吧，联邦法律，无论是宪法、联邦成文法还是联邦条约，在遇到任何与之冲突的州法时都具有最高效力。

sentences.en: So the idea here is that you have this very important structural part of the constitution, that federal law is supreme.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的核心理念是，宪法中存在这样一个非常重要的结构性部分，即联邦法律至高无上。

sentences.en: So what does that mean, practically speaking?
sentences.zh: 那么，从实际角度来看，这意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, what that means is if you can think of supremacy as stating the simple fact that federal law is supreme,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着，如果你把“至高”理解为阐明了联邦法律至高无上这一简单事实，

sentences.en: but arising out of supremacy is the idea that Congress now has the power when it legislates to preempt, or that really means displace or override any contrary state or local law.
sentences.zh: 但从“至高”中衍生出的概念是，国会在立法时现在拥有了先发制人的权力，这实际上意味着取代或凌驾于任何相反的州或地方法律之上。

sentences.en: So you can think of preemption as being based in the constitutional power of supremacy.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以认为“先发制人”根植于至高无上的宪法权力之中。

sentences.en: So Congress doesn't have to exercise preemption, but when it does pass laws in this way, it's very clear that any directly conflicting state or local law has to give way.
sentences.zh: 因此，国会不必非得行使优先权，但当它以这种方式通过法律时，很明显，任何与之直接冲突的州或地方法律都必须让路。

sentences.en: So that's kind of the genius or the simplicity of the Supremacy Clause.
sentences.zh: 这就是至高条款的精妙或简单之处。

sentences.en: But that's the most simple part of the Supremacy Clause.
sentences.zh: 但这是至高条款最简单的部分。

sentences.en: And I take it, there's lots of constitutional case law based on the Supremacy Clause.
sentences.zh: 我猜，基于至高条款还有大量的宪法判例法吧。

sentences.en: That's right, because things can never be simple, right?
sentences.zh: 没错，因为事情永远不可能那么简单，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So when you think about federal law, sometimes Congress can simply say, we're going to pass a law, and this law will, in the text of the law itself,
sentences.zh: 所以当你想到联邦法律时，有时国会可以简单地说：我们要通过一项法律，并且这项法律将在法律文本本身中，

sentences.en: displace or preempt any similar state law.
sentences.zh: 取代或优先于任何类似的州法。

sentences.en: That's pretty easy.
sentences.zh: 那挺容易的。

sentences.en: And if that were the only issue, we'd never talk about preemption, right?
sentences.zh: 如果这真的是唯一的问题，我们就永远不会讨论优先权了，对吧？

sentences.en: But the problem is that Congress very often doesn't say.
sentences.zh: 但问题是国会往往不会这么说。

sentences.en: There may be a federal law on a topic and a state law on a topic, and the federal law doesn't say anything.
sentences.zh: 某个议题可能同时存在联邦法律和州法律，而联邦法律什么也没说。

sentences.en: So in response, the Supreme Court has come up with a whole host of cases, doctrines, tests, ways of thinking about federal preemption to try and answer the question,
sentences.zh: 因此，作为回应，最高法院想出了大量的案件、学说、测试方法以及思考联邦优先权的方式，试图回答这样一个问题：

sentences.en: what happens when it seems like there are federal and state laws legislating on the same topic?
sentences.zh: 当看起来有联邦和州法律在同一议题上进行立法时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: So what exactly is supposed to happen when there's a conflict?
sentences.zh: 那么发生冲突时究竟应该发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, that also is a complicated answer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也是一个复杂的答案。

sentences.en: So it depends on what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于我们在谈论什么。

sentences.en: Sometimes courts will say something like, you know, there are some areas of federal law where the federal interest is so important, so extreme,
sentences.zh: 有时法院会说这样的话：你知道的，在联邦法律的某些领域，联邦利益是如此重要、如此极端，

sentences.en: we don't want the states to get involved a little tiny bit even, even if Congress hasn't specifically spoken to that area.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望各州哪怕插手一点点，即使国会没有明确谈及该领域。

sentences.en: So an interest like this would be foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 像这样的利益比如外交政策。

sentences.en: We don't want the states to get involved with foreign policy, negotiating their own treaties.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望各州介入外交政策、去谈判他们自己的条约。

sentences.en: That would be a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 那会是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: That would be a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 那会是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So those are the easy cases.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是简单的案件。

sentences.en: But the much more frequent and difficult cases are sometimes courts have to answer, well, there's a federal law on a topic and a state law on the topic.
sentences.zh: 但更常见、更困难的案件是，法院有时必须回答：某个议题既有联邦法又有州法，

sentences.en: Is it possible to comply with both state and federal law?
sentences.zh: 是否有可能同时遵守州法和联邦法？

sentences.en: If it's possible, maybe there is no preemption.
sentences.zh: 如果可能的话，也许就不存在优先权冲突。

sentences.en: No preemption would mean that state law and federal law are both valid.
sentences.zh: 没有优先权冲突就意味着州法和联邦法都有效。

sentences.en: But, for instance, if there is a way in which the state law is an obstacle for the federal government's law to operate, or whether it's literally impossible,
sentences.zh: 但是，举例来说，如果州法在某种程度上成为了联邦政府法律运作的障碍，或者是否字面上完全不可能，

sentences.en: state law says black and federal law says white, you can't do both at the same time, then that's a case of federal preemption.
sentences.zh: 州法说黑色而联邦法说白色，你无法同时做到这两点，那么这就是联邦优先权适用的情况。

sentences.en: So these are always case-by-case determinations.
sentences.zh: 所以这些总是需要逐案进行判定。

sentences.en: But preemption is actually really important because if you think about all of the different areas in which the federal government regulates, everything from the environment,
sentences.zh: 但优先权实际上非常重要，因为如果你想想联邦政府监管的所有不同领域，从环境、

sentences.en: consumer protection, energy, you name it, the states also often legislate in the same areas.
sentences.zh: 消费者保护、能源，应有尽有，各州也经常在这些相同的领域进行立法。

sentences.en: And what you will have are individuals or companies that say, well, I want to comply with one, I don't want to comply with both, or am I supposed to comply with both?
sentences.zh: 然后你就会遇到个人或公司说：好吧，我想遵守其中一个，我不想两个都遵守，或者我到底该不该两个都遵守？

sentences.en: And that gives rise to preemption.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了优先权问题。

sentences.en: So of all of the areas of law that we've talked about with the Constitution, in fact, preemption is probably the most frequently used constitutional law in practice.

sentences.zh: 然后在生成式人工智能领域，由于我部分时间住在纽约市，亚当斯政府花了，你知道的，差不多，我想，

sentences.en: And then in the generative AI space, because I live partly in New York City, the Adams administration spent, you know, nearly, I think,

sentences.en: a million dollars on this government chat bot, this NYC bot or NYC chat that was supposed to, you know, the idea of it was good.
sentences.zh: 但它却在指导他们违法。
