sentences.en: And, you know, I think well beyond the kind of whimsical term, you know, hallucination that we use that, you know, often suggests that it's not a really big deal.
sentences.zh: 但这些令人担忧的方面，我认为也让你体会到，在我们生活的方方面面，

sentences.en: And, you know, we shouldn't be surprised that I think the Mamdani administration, I think, canceled that contract and got rid of the chat bot.
sentences.zh: 所有这些地方都在同时受到某种形式的算法决策或管理的塑造。

sentences.en: But the concerning aspects, I think, also just give you a sense of, like, all of the places in our lives,
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: all of the sites simultaneously that are being shaped in some way by some form of kind of algorithmic decision making or management.
sentences.zh: 我想处理这个问题的方法之一，对吧，就是不能仅仅说，哦，这些都是技术问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但既然你提到，个人可能会在各种不同的方面感到无力或对所发生的事情感到困惑，

sentences.en: And I guess one of the ways to approach that, right, is to say not just like, oh, these are technical probleMs.
sentences.zh: 你某种程度上可以使用民权的方法。

sentences.en: But since you're mentioning, like, all of the different ways that individuals might feel powerless or just confused about what's going on,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当然，在拜登政府期间，你领导了白宫科技政策办公室（OSTP）。

sentences.en: you can kind of use a civil rights approach.
sentences.zh: 人们认为你领导制定了白宫的《人工智能权利法案蓝图》。

sentences.en: And, you know, and of course, in the Biden administration, you led the OSTP.
sentences.zh: 我很想听你多谈谈这个。

sentences.en: And you're credited with directing the White House blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.
sentences.zh: 这是一个，你知道的，这是一份政策文件。

sentences.en: And I would love for you to talk more about that.
sentences.zh: 这是一份白皮书。

sentences.en: There is a, you know, this is a policy paper.
sentences.zh: 那么这个过程是怎样的？

sentences.en: It's a white paper.
sentences.zh: 你是如何开始创建这个蓝图的？

sentences.en: So what was the process?
sentences.zh: 比如，幕后有哪些人？

sentences.en: How did you begin creating the blueprint?
sentences.zh: 你都和谁交谈过？

sentences.en: Like, who was behind it?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who did you talk to?
sentences.zh: 我也想知道

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 更多细节。

sentences.en: So it was, you know, we came into office in the middle of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是，你知道的，我们在大流行期间上台。

sentences.en: And we came into office as a country having a racial reckoning.
sentences.zh: 我们上台时，国家正经历一场种族清算。

sentences.en: We were having an economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正经历一场经济危机。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: I think those of us who work in the science and technology policy space knew both on the research side and also kind of saw brewing amidst all of these kind of societal concerns,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们这些从事科学和技术政策领域工作的人，无论是在研究方面，还是在看到所有这些社会关切中酝酿的问题时，

sentences.en: like what was going to be happening in the algorithmic space.
sentences.zh: 比如算法领域将会发生什么。

sentences.en: And we all, you know, we were having already examples.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都，你知道的，我们已经有了实例。

sentences.en: So, for example, the YouTube videos about, you know, the so-called racist soap dispensers and faucets.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，关于YouTube上那些所谓种族歧视的肥皂分配器和水龙头视频。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: You know, if you have darker skin, you can't get the soap to come out, which is a kind of application of AI.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你的肤色较深，你就无法让肥皂流出来，这可以说是AI的一种应用。

sentences.en: And, you know, and I had the idea to do, in part, I think, you know, borrowed from lots of other examples.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我产生这个想法，部分原因我认为，你知道的，借鉴了许多其他例子。

sentences.en: I mean, the Obama administration accompanied its Affordable Care Act with something called the Patients Bill of Rights.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，奥巴马政府在推行《平价医疗法案》时，伴随着一项名为《患者权利法案》的东西。

sentences.en: I think Ralph Nader had a Consumer Bill of Rights.
sentences.zh: 我想拉尔夫·纳德曾提出过一个《消费者权利法案》。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the Bill of Rights has been used, you know, variously, both by government and in folks in civil society,
sentences.zh: 所以权利法案曾被各种各样地使用，你知道的，无论是政府还是公民社会的人士，

sentences.en: as a way to sort of think about a rights expansion in the face of kind of a new technology or a new social dynamic, for example.
sentences.zh: 将其作为一种方式，在面对新技术或新社会动态时，思考如何扩展权利，例如。

sentences.en: So we got into office by October of 2021.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在2021年10月之前上台。

sentences.en: We published an op-ed and Wired that came out in October of 2021.
sentences.zh: 我们在2021年10月在《连线》杂志上发表了一篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: And we sort of used the Bill of Rights framing and we kind of tried to draw a parallel to the country's founding and noting that there was this time, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们采用了权利法案的框架，并试图将其与国家的建国历史进行平行对比，指出曾有过这样一个时期，你知道的，

sentences.en: in the 1780s and 90s that Americans adopted the original Bill of Rights to guard against really a power.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪80和90年代，美国人通过了最初的权利法案，以真正防范某种权力。

sentences.en: They just created this powerful government, right?
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚创建了这个强大的政府，对吧？

sentences.en: We're about to celebrate the 250 years of the Declaration of Independence and then the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我们即将庆祝《独立宣言》发表250周年，然后是《宪法》。

sentences.en: Like, we had created this kind of powerful government technology and that we needed to place a check on that.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们创造了这种强大的政府技术，我们需要对其实施制约。

sentences.en: So how did you secure our rights and our liberties, our opportunities in the context of a kind of large and powerful government?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这样一个庞大且强大的政府背景下，你如何保障我们的权利、自由和机会？

sentences.en: So we saw a parallel with the kind of powerful technologies and the powerful companies that were pushing these powerful technologies and thought that there was a useful analogy and were wanting to think with the public,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到了强大技术以及推动这些强大技术的强大公司之间的相似之处，并认为这是一个有用的类比，我们希望与公众，

sentences.en: with the American public, about what might be equivalent kind of guardrails against these kind of new powerful domains.
sentences.zh: 与美国公众一起思考，针对这些新的强大领域，什么样的护栏才算是同等水平的。

sentences.en: And so we were trying to kind of frame the blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights project within a kind of continuous, you know, U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图将《AI权利法案蓝图》项目构建于一种连续的、你知道的，美国，

sentences.en: or American tradition of aspiring to values, kind of recognizing the shortcomings of the systems that we create and sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 或是美国的传统之中，即追求各种价值观，认识到我们所创造系统的缺点，并且，你知道的，

sentences.en: thinking about what we might do to sort of mitigate it.
sentences.zh: 思考我们可以做些什么来减轻这种影响。

sentences.en: Can you tell us some of the five principles that are identified in the AI Bill of Rights?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们讲讲《AI权利法案》中确定的那五个原则中的一些吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we, so the five principles was, and the white paper that Elizabeth alluded to was released in October of 2022, so a year later.
sentences.zh: 所以我们，这五个原则是——伊丽莎白刚才提到的白皮书是在2022年10月发布的，也就是一年后。

sentences.en: And what we did over the course of that year was a lot of public engagement.
sentences.zh: 在那一年里，我们做了大量的公众参与工作。

sentences.en: So we had that wired op-ed ends with an email address that can go direct, that you can write to the White House.
sentences.zh: 所以我们那篇《连线》专栏文章的结尾提供了一个可以直接联系白宫的电子邮箱。

sentences.en: That's always a good plan.
sentences.zh: 这总是一个好主意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think we wish more people had taken us up on it, but people certainly did.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们希望更多的人能接受我们的建议，但确实有人这么做了。

sentences.en: And we did kind of focus groups.
sentences.zh: 我们还举行了焦点小组座谈会。

sentences.en: We had what we called office hours.
sentences.zh: 我们有所谓的开放办公时间。

sentences.en: So everybody who worked on the team, which included policy generalists, AI scientists, computer scientists, folks who work on science and technology policy from academia,
sentences.zh: 因此，团队里的每个人，包括政策多面手、AI科学家、计算机科学家、来自学术界从事科技政策工作的人员，

sentences.en: who had government experience, who had commercial experience.
sentences.zh: 他们有政府经验，也有商业经验。

sentences.en: So it was a pretty broad team.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个相当多元的团队。

sentences.en: And we would all block on our calendar time just to talk with people.
sentences.zh: 我们会在日历上预留时间，专门与人们交谈。

sentences.en: And that included high school students and rabbis, in addition to always the technology companies, lobbyists, you know.
sentences.zh: 除了历来都有的技术公司和游说集团之外，其中还包括高中生和拉比，你知道的。

sentences.en: But we really tried to have a broad conversation.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实努力展开了广泛的对话。

sentences.en: And what we, so the five principles are really distilled from those conversations.
sentences.zh: 所以，这五个原则实际上是从这些对话中提炼出来的。

sentences.en: We don't, we weren't trying to do anything novel.
sentences.zh: 我们没有，我们并没有试图去做什么新奇的事情。

sentences.en: We were trying to sort of take from these, this near year of conversation, like, what is the best of what we think?
sentences.zh: 我们只是试图从近一年的对话中汲取：我们认为最好的是什么？

sentences.en: What are the aspirations that we should have as we move as a society into a more kind of algorithmic shaped mediated world?
sentences.zh: 当我们的社会迈向一个更加由算法塑造和媒介化的世界时，我们应该抱有什么样的愿景？

sentences.en: So, one was that AI systems should be safe and effective.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，AI系统应该是安全和有效的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a very kind of basic and almost kind of consumer rights principle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常基础且几乎属于消费者权益的原则。

sentences.en: Second, that people should have protections from algorithmic discrimination.
sentences.zh: 第二，人们应该得到保护，免受算法歧视。

sentences.en: Third, that there should be, you know, some modicum of data privacy.
sentences.zh: 第三，应该存在，你知道的，某种程度的数据隐私。

sentences.en: We are still fighting out what that might even look like.
sentences.zh: 我们仍在争论这到底会是什么样子。

sentences.en: But, again, these are kind of aspirations.
sentences.zh: 但是，再次说明，这些都是一种愿景。

sentences.en: Fourth, that there should be notice and explanation so that you should have a right to know when an AI system is being used to make consequential decisions.
sentences.zh: 第四，应该有知情和解释权，这样当AI系统被用于做出具有重大影响的决策时，你有权知道。

sentences.en: Like some of those that I was talking about, Elizabeth, when you asked me what's concerning.
sentences.zh: 就像伊丽莎白你问我什么是令人担忧的时候，我谈到的其中一些那样。

sentences.en: Like, you know, do we care if you get a bad Netflix recommendation and you end up watching a movie you don't really like that the algorithm told you you were going to like?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，如果我们给你一个糟糕的Netflix推荐，最后你看了一部算法告诉你你会喜欢但实际上你并不喜欢的电影，我们在乎吗？

sentences.en: Like, no.
sentences.zh: 完全不在乎。

sentences.en: But when algorithms and more, you know, advanced AI systems are being made for consequential decisions about people's lives, they should know about that.
sentences.zh: 但是，当算法以及更多，你知道的，先进的AI系统被用于对人们的生活做出重大决策时，他们应该知情。

sentences.en: And if they want an explanation, they should be able to get one.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想要一个解释，他们应该能够得到一个。

sentences.en: And then, lastly, the last principle is that there should be some sort of human alternative or fallback so that you should, you know, ideally be able to opt out.
sentences.zh: 然后，最后，最后一个原则是应该某种形式的人工替代方案或后备机制，这样你，你知道的，理想情况下应该能够选择退出。

sentences.en: We build a lot of algorithm and social media systems as opt-in as opposed to opting people out.
sentences.zh: 我们构建了许多算法和社交媒体系统，采用的是默认加入（opt-in）而不是默认退出（opt-out）。

sentences.en: So, can you opt out of an automated system?
sentences.zh: 所以，你能退出一个自动化系统吗？

sentences.en: Can you talk to a real person instead of being kind of brought down into a circle of like a phone tree hell where you keep trying to press zero to get to a person?
sentences.zh: 你能和一个真人对话，而不是被拉进类似电话树地狱的循环中，不停地按零试图找到一个活人吗？

sentences.en: Particularly when it's about something that affects your life.
sentences.zh: 特别是在涉及影响你生活的事情时。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, health insurance, jobs, housing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，健康保险、工作、住房。

sentences.en: So, these are really critical things.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些都是非常关键的事情。

sentences.en: So, that's what we came up with.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们得出的结论。

sentences.en: And it's been, you know, variously sort of taken up by different kinds of constituencies.
sentences.zh: 而且它已经被，你知道的，不同的选民群体以各种方式采纳了。

sentences.en: It's become a kind of a civic infrastructure that is a way, I think, that allows different kinds of communities, particularly non-expert communities,
sentences.zh: 它已经成为了一种公民基础设施，我认为，这让不同的社区，特别是缺乏专业知识的社区，

sentences.en: to talk about why AI is important and how they want it to sort of sit in their lives and not sit in their lives.
sentences.zh: 能够讨论为什么AI很重要，以及他们希望AI如何存在于他们的生活中，或者不希望它存在于他们的生活中。

sentences.en: So, from, you know, from an ordinary person's perspective, what would it mean to have a safe AI system?
sentences.zh: 那么，从，你知道的，普通人的角度来看，拥有一个安全的AI系统意味着什么？

sentences.en: Does it mean that it's not going to make mistakes or is it, you know, what do you envision as like an AI system that would follow this idea of safety?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着它不会犯错，或者说，你知道的，你所设想的遵循这种安全理念的AI系统是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, my friend Damon, who leads the Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我的朋友达蒙（Damon），他领导着民权律师委员会，你知道的，

sentences.en: he will often say there's more laws around your toaster than around the chatbot that you might have used this morning, which is true.
sentences.zh: 他经常说，关于你烤面包机的法律比关于你今天早上可能用过的聊天机器人的法律还要多，这是事实。

sentences.en: So, we just basically don't have, certainly at a federal level, there's some action happening at the state level, but any kind of just basic consumer protection.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们基本上没有，当然在联邦层面没有，州层面有一些行动，但缺乏任何形式的基本消费者保护。

sentences.en: So, I think many people are actually shocked when they realize that when, you know, an AI company or a tech company sort of ships a new model or an update of a model,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为许多人在意识到当，你知道的，一家AI公司或科技公司推出一个新模型或模型的更新时，

sentences.en: that no one has looked at that.
sentences.zh: 竟然没有人审查过它，都会感到震惊。

sentences.en: There's been no kind of third-party kind of authority that said, you know, it's met some threshold or standard of testing and that we think it should be safe and effective.
sentences.zh: 没有任何第三方机构说，你知道的，它达到了某种测试的门槛或标准，我们认为它应该是安全和有效的。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are affordances, there are things about, particularly about generative AI,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，有一些特性，有一些关于生成式AI的特性，

sentences.en: and we know increasingly from the research that you're never going to get rid of all of the mistakes in generative AI, certainly not in large language models.
sentences.zh: 而且我们从研究中越来越清楚地知道，你永远无法消除生成式AI中的所有错误，在大语言模型中更是如此。

sentences.en: So, safe and effective systems doesn't mean that,
sentences.zh: 所以，安全和有效的系统并不意味着那样，

sentences.en: but it does mean that one should expect that there should be testing on what people think would be the most obvious use cases of these technologies, right?
sentences.zh: 但它确实意味着人们应该期望，对这些技术最显而易见的用例进行测试，对吧？

sentences.en: You can't, if it's a multifunction or a multi-use technology, there are use cases, I think, that we can't, we haven't even imagined and people aren't doing yet.
sentences.zh: 你不能，如果它是一种多功能或多用途的技术，有些用例，我认为，是我们甚至无法想象、人们也尚未开始做的。

sentences.en: But, I think anybody who has studied the history of technology in the United States, even just going back to the 90s, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，我认为任何研究过美国技术史的人，哪怕只是追溯到90年代，你知道的，

sentences.en: we know there's always going to be a problem with scams, scamming, and fraud.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，诈骗和欺诈问题总是会存在。

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 永远如此。

sentences.en: Any kind of new technology.
sentences.zh: 任何新技术都是如此。

sentences.en: We know historically there's always going to be a problem with forms of, you know, pornography, sexual abuse.
sentences.zh: 我们从历史上知道，某种形式的，你知道的，色情、性虐待问题也总是会存在。

sentences.en: These things are, like, often the first use cases for new technologies.
sentences.zh: 这些事情，就像，通常是新技术最初的用例。

sentences.en: And so, you know, that we have chatbots that are being used to nudify young people in high school or on rock or whatever, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们现在有的聊天机器人被用来对高中或摇滚乐等领域的年轻人进行脱衣换脸（nudify），比如，

sentences.en: we can't act like these are not harmful use cases that were not anticipated.
sentences.zh: 我们不能装作这些不是有害的、且本可预见的用例。

sentences.en: And so, it doesn't mean at all, Elizabeth, that there won't be unanticipated things or that, you know, that a chatbot won't hallucinate.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊丽莎白，这绝不意味着不会出现意料之外的事情，或者说，你知道的，聊天机器人不会产生幻觉。

sentences.en: But it certainly should mean that a company, before releasing a product,
sentences.zh: 但它绝对意味着一家公司在发布产品之前，

sentences.en: has thought through even basic historical use cases and actually thought about how they might be mitigated or that, you know,
sentences.zh: 已经思考过哪怕是最基础的历史用例，并真正思考过如何减轻这些危害，或者说，你知道的，

sentences.en: should have a conversation about some independent stakeholder, you know, state government, you know, a civil society.
sentences.zh: 应该与某个独立的利益相关者，你知道的，州政府，你知道的，公民社会进行对话。

sentences.en: I don't, you know, about how they might be mitigated.
sentences.zh: 我不，你知道的，关于如何减轻这些危害进行对话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, you'd think with all this, essentially, you're sort of describing this experimentation, right, that's happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你会认为有了这一切，基本上你是在描述这种正在发生的实验，对吧？

sentences.en: And we'd expect that if the government's going to do this, they also should be regulating it a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们会期望，如果政府要这样做，他们也应该对其进行大量的监管。

sentences.en: And the answer at the federal level has been crickets, mostly.
sentences.zh: 而在联邦层面，得到的回答基本上一片寂静。

sentences.en: There has been some movement.
sentences.zh: 也有一些进展。

sentences.en: I mean, the Blueprint served as a springboard for President Biden's executive order on AI.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这份蓝图成为了拜登总统关于AI的行政命令的跳板。

sentences.en: So, could you say a little bit about what the core of those concerns were in the EO?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能简单谈谈该行政命令中这些关切的核心是什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I think the philosophy, both for the AI Bill of Rights and for the most part for President Biden's executive order on AI,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为无论对于《AI权利法案》还是很大程度上的拜登总统AI行政命令而言，其哲学都在于，

sentences.en: was that just because we have a new technology does not mean that we have to have a new social compact or a new social contract.
sentences.zh: 不能仅仅因为我们有了新技术，就意味着我们必须建立一个新的社会契约或社会合同。

sentences.en: Like, you don't have to throw out every policy, regulation, and law because we have this new technology as powerful as it may be.
sentences.zh: 就像，你不能因为有了这项无论多么强大的新技术，就把所有的政策、规章和法律都扔掉一样。

sentences.en: So, if intentional discrimination or intentional violations of people's civil rights or liberties are illegal in any other fashion, if you do that with AI, it's also illegal,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果蓄意歧视或蓄意侵犯人们的公民权利或自由在任何其他情况下都是非法的，如果你用AI来做这件事，它同样是非法的，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You might have to differently figure out the mechanism or differently make the case, but the outcome is, you know, the legality of the outcome is the same.
sentences.zh: 你可能需要用不同的方式弄清楚机制或提出不同的论点，但结果是，你知道的，结果的合法性是一样的。

sentences.en: One of the things the executive order did was ask the Department of Education to think about what, you know,
sentences.zh: 该行政命令做的事情之一是要求教育部思考，你知道的，

sentences.en: you've got guidelines for children's privacy and their protection for the use of educational technology.
sentences.zh: 你们已经有了关于儿童隐私以及在教育技术中使用儿童保护的指南。

sentences.en: Do those need to be updated or how do we need to,
sentences.zh: 这些需要更新吗，或者我们需要如何做，

sentences.en: or do we just need to double down on what we have as you're introducing different forms of advanced AI potentially to the classroom, right?
sentences.zh: 还是说，随着你们可能将各种形式的先进AI引入课堂，我们需要加倍贯彻现有的规定，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, the president's executive order had some, you know, directions to things like the Department of Labor.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，总统的行政命令对诸如劳工部等机构做出了一些，你知道的，指示。

sentences.en: And I think differently from what the current administration has been doing, it was not just what is AI going to do to work?
sentences.zh: 我认为与现任政府一直在做的事情不同，它不仅仅关注AI会对工作产生什么影响，

sentences.en: It was how can government help put speed bumps or friction or help to direct the sort of direction of travel?
sentences.zh: 它还关注政府如何帮助设置减速带、摩擦力，或者帮助引导发展方向？

sentences.en: So you're not just potentially casting people out of work, you are helping them find other work, you are re-skilling them.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不只是可能把人们赶出工作岗位，你还在帮助他们找到其他工作，帮他们重新掌握技能。

sentences.en: Could there be a conversation about tax incentives or other kinds of incentives to keep people on work or to help people off board or on ramp to different work, for example?
sentences.zh: 例如，是否可以讨论税收优惠或其他类型的激励措施，以让人保住工作，或者帮助人们平稳过渡或转向不同的工作？

sentences.en: The executive order, of course, also weighed in on, you know, there was a lot of concern and remains a lot of concern in the national security space.
sentences.zh: 当然，该行政命令还权衡了，你知道的，国家安全领域存在着并且依然存在着大量的关切。

sentences.en: So, you know, should there be export control?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，应该有出口管制吗？

sentences.en: Should we be controlling where various forms of technology go?
sentences.zh: 我们是否应该控制各种技术的流向？

sentences.en: So this is still a very live conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以这仍然是一个非常现实的讨论。

sentences.en: Controversially, the executive order proposed that we would use the Defense Production Act from, I think,
sentences.zh: 充满争议的是，该行政命令提议我们动用，我认为，最初来自二战时期的《国防生产法》，

sentences.en: World War II originally to require that companies give the government more input and information about new,
sentences.zh: 要求公司向政府提供更多关于新型、更强大的AI系统和工具的输入和信息，

sentences.en: more powerful AI systems and tools that had a kind of certain threshold of capability.
sentences.zh: 这些系统和工具达到了某种特定的能力门槛。

sentences.en: So it was, it might have been historically the longest executive order ever.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能是历史上最长的行政命令。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I think it was a hundred and some pages, a hundred and one or a hundred and two.
sentences.zh: 我想它有一百多页，101页或102页。

sentences.en: You know, as a reformist, a reformer, I don't necessarily think that is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为一个改革者，我并不一定认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: You know, in some ways it's a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面这其实是一件坏事。

sentences.en: But in this case, I think it was good in the sense that it tried to be comprehensive, that the philosophy here was that this is a kind of new infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，我认为它是好的，因为它试图做到全面，这里的哲学是，这是一种新的基础设施。

sentences.en: This is sort of a new operating system for a lot of the work that we do and how might we think about the ways that government can both help to accelerate potential good use cases and mitigate potential harms using the things,
sentences.zh: 这有点像我们所做的大多数工作的一个新操作系统，我们如何思考政府可以利用机构和行政部门已经具备的事物、工具、机制和杠杆，

sentences.en: the tools, the mechanisms, the levers that government agencies and the executive already have.
sentences.zh: 既能加速潜在的良好用例，又能减轻潜在的危害。

sentences.en: We're going to take a break, but when we come back, we'll turn to how the federal government is and isn't regulating AI and how the states are filling in the gaps.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下，但回来后，我们将探讨联邦政府是如何以及没有如何监管AI的，以及各州是如何填补这些空白的。

sentences.en: So before the break, we talked to Dr. Alondra Nelson about how to think about artificial intelligence and why it poses a risk and should be regulated.
sentences.zh: 所以在休息前，我们采访了阿隆德拉·纳尔逊（Alondra Nelson）博士，探讨了如何看待人工智能，以及为什么它会带来风险并应该受到监管。

sentences.en: And so how did her work lead to a conversation about preemption?
sentences.zh: 那么她的工作是如何引发关于先占权（preemption）的讨论的呢？

sentences.en: Well, as she's already mentioned, during her time in the Biden White House, she helped create the blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.
sentences.zh: 正如她已经提到的那样，在拜登白宫任职期间，她帮助创建了《AI权利法案蓝图》。

sentences.en: And that blueprint became the impetus for a part of President Biden's 2023 executive order on AI.
sentences.zh: 而那个蓝图成为了拜登总统2023年AI行政命令一部分的推动力。

sentences.en: And as she's already discussed, that order told the federal agencies to address the safe and ethical use of AI.
sentences.zh: 正如她已经讨论过的，该行政命令指示联邦机构解决AI的安全和道德使用问题。

sentences.en: Now, that's the limit of what President Biden can do.
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是拜登所能做到的极限。

sentences.en: And that's because Congress has the power to legislate, not the president.
sentences.zh: 这是因为国会有立法权，而总统没有。

sentences.en: So while Biden could tell the executive branch what to do about AI, he lacked the authority to actually preempt state law.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然拜登可以告诉行政分支如何处理AI，但他缺乏实际先占（preempt）州法的权力。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And as soon as he began his second term, Trump rescinded or did away with Biden's executive order and replaced it with his own.
sentences.zh: 而且他一开启第二个任期，特朗普就废除了拜登的行政命令，并用他自己的行政命令取而代之。

sentences.en: Now, the Trump administration's approach to AI has been to turn away from a focus on safety and ethics in AI.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府对待人工智能的方法，一直是转移人们对人工智能的安全性和伦理问题的关注。

sentences.en: Surprise, surprise.
sentences.zh: 这可真是意料之外呢。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And instead, to focus on what the federal government can do to accelerate AI development.
sentences.zh: 转而关注联邦政府能做些什么来加速人工智能的发展。

sentences.en: Now, Trump's executive order has called upon Congress to use its power of preemption, based in the Supremacy Clause, to override state laws on AI.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的行政命令呼吁国会利用基于联邦至高条款的优先权权力，来推翻各州关于人工智能的法律。

sentences.en: Congress so far has not responded.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，国会还没有作出回应。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Which has left a lot of room for the states.
sentences.zh: 这就给各州留下了很大的空间。

sentences.en: And so we'll pick up our conversation there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从这里继续探讨。

sentences.en: So we have a lot of different states regulating on AI.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们有很多不同的州在对人工智能进行监管。

sentences.en: You know, California has been in the lead, as it often is in these areas.
sentences.zh: 你知道，加利福尼亚州一直走在前列，在这个领域它通常都是这样。

sentences.en: You know, so, for example, California has just a lot of different laws on AI.
sentences.zh: 比如说，加利福尼亚州出台了许多不同的人工智能法律。

sentences.en: For example, you know, you've got to disclose what kind of data you use if you're an AI developer, what you use to train your models.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你是一名人工智能开发者，你必须披露你使用的数据类型，以及你用来训练模型的数据。

sentences.en: That seems like very technical, very big picture.
sentences.zh: 这听起来非常技术化，也十分宏观。

sentences.en: There's also some very specific California laws that we just passed a law.
sentences.zh: 还有一些非常具体的加州法律，我们刚刚通过了一项法律。

sentences.en: You know, if you're a police department, you've got to disclose if you use generative AI when your officers write their police reports.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是一个警察局，当警员撰写警方报告时，如果使用了生成式人工智能，你必须进行披露。

sentences.en: That's a good one.
sentences.zh: 这倒是个不错的规定。

sentences.en: So you've got the whole range of different things.
sentences.zh: 所以你面临着各种各样不同的情况。

sentences.en: So what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那么这意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: You talk to a lot of people in the industry.
sentences.zh: 你和业内许多人交谈过。

sentences.en: If I'm an AI developer and I want to offer my product in California or I want to offer my product in Colorado, which has an algorithmic discrimination law,
sentences.zh: 如果我是一名人工智能开发者，我想在加利福尼亚州推出我的产品，或者我想在科罗拉多州推出我的产品（该州有一项算法歧视法），

sentences.en: what does that even mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 这该如何运作？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think the first thing to say is that it's that we have other industries, you know, where you have different kinds of regulations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，首先要说明的是，在其他行业中，你知道的，也存在着各种不同类型的监管。

sentences.en: So you've got like, you know, insurance is like regulated mostly by the states, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，保险业主要就是由各州监管的，例如。

sentences.en: We've talked about a little bit consumer protection.
sentences.zh: 我们之前稍微讨论过消费者保护。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, I think the discourse that gets used in D.C., which is its own language of its own,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我认为华盛顿特区所使用的那些论调，其实有着它自己的一套话语体系，

sentences.en: there's a lot of kind of like pearl clutching around the fact that you would have different laws in different states.
sentences.zh: 对于不同州会有不同法律这件事，大家多少都有点大惊小怪。

sentences.en: Although the same, very same people in Washington, because they are the most adept people on, you know, what the regulatory space looks like more broadly writ large, like,
sentences.zh: 尽管华盛顿的那些人，由于他们是最精通监管领域在更广泛意义上是如何运作的行家里手，

sentences.en: you know, know that it's true all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们其实一直都知道这是真的。

sentences.en: You know, it's basically true.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这基本是事实。

sentences.en: And I think there's like, you know, there's real, we use the phrase, you know, laboratories of democracy.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正如我们常说的那样，存在着所谓的“民主实验室”。

sentences.en: I think there's something to that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种说法是有道理的。

sentences.en: I mean, you have a new technology that I think is fast moving.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一项我认为发展迅速的新技术。

sentences.en: I think in some ideal demos, would you want just one, you know, a rule, you know, a law to rule them all?
sentences.zh: 我想在某些理想的民主政体中，你会希望只有一条规则，你知道的，一个统领一切的法律吗？

sentences.en: Sure, right.
sentences.zh: 当然，没错。

sentences.en: But we don't live in that ideal demos.
sentences.zh: 但我们并不生活在那种理想的民主政体中。

sentences.en: And we also know that the states are much closer to the harMs.
sentences.zh: 而且我们也知道，各州距离实际伤害更近。

sentences.en: Like, so you also have to imagine being a governor of a state or a state legislator or senator in a state,
sentences.zh: 所以，你还得想象一下作为一个州的州长、州议员或参议员会是什么感觉，

sentences.en: and you have people writing to you about being worried about the future of their children.
sentences.zh: 你会收到人们写来的信件，表达他们对孩子未来的担忧。

sentences.en: You know, we had a scandal, I'm sitting here in Princeton and New Jersey about nudify apps.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我在普林斯顿和新泽西这里就遇到过关于“脱衣”应用的丑闻。

sentences.en: Like, you know, lots of just, I think, concerns about, you know, reading in the news and experiencing young people harming themselves.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，有很多这样的担忧，从新闻中读到，也亲历年轻人受到伤害。

sentences.en: You know, there's been something I saw a case reported about a potential homicide.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我曾看到过一则关于潜在谋杀案的报道。

sentences.en: And I think if you are a state legislator and you're hearing from constituents who've been denied a mortgage or screened out of a job by an algorithm,
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你是一名州议员，并且听到选民反映他们因算法而被拒绝发放抵押贷款或在求职中被筛掉，

sentences.en: you can't just sit blithely and sort of not respond to that.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是无动于衷地坐视不管，对这种事毫无反应。

sentences.en: So I think partly it's just like folks are hearing it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为部分原因只是大家都在听到这些声音。

sentences.en: I think that we have a new technology.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们面对的是一项新技术。

sentences.en: What are the best ways to think about this?
sentences.zh: 思考这个问题的最好方式是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, even with the case, you mentioned California and New York,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，哪怕就你提到的加利福尼亚州和纽约州的案例来看，

sentences.en: which have done laws around kind of trying to require some disclosure and transparency from companies around harMs.
sentences.zh: 它们已经围绕试图要求企业就相关危害进行一些信息披露和透明度立法做出了举措。

sentences.en: Texas is, you know, has weighed in actually on thinking about harms and including discrimination.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州，你知道的，实际上也权衡并考虑了危害问题，包括歧视。

sentences.en: But they've said it really has to be intent.
sentences.zh: 但他们表示，这必须是主观故意的。

sentences.en: It can't be if there's unintentional harms, you know, that they're trying to let the companies off the hook.
sentences.zh: 不能说如果是无意造成的伤害，你知道的，他们就想让企业逃避责任。

sentences.en: You know, a place like Colorado has attempted the first, you know, we might think of as like an omnibus AI bill that covers lots of things, you know,
sentences.zh: 像科罗拉多州这样的地方，已经尝试了我们可能会认为是第一部综合性人工智能法案的东西，涵盖了许多内容，你知道的，

sentences.en: including sort of harms to young people, deep fakes, discrimination.
sentences.zh: 包括对青少年的伤害、深度伪造以及歧视。

sentences.en: And these are all these are like I've just named three different approaches and it's not clear which one of those is the best one or which one's going to be most efficacious.
sentences.zh: 这些全都是——我刚刚列举了三种不同的方法，目前还不清楚其中哪一种是最好的，或者哪一种最有效。

sentences.en: And I think it's worth actually letting states do this, you know, finish the work of implementing these laws and actually find out.
sentences.zh: 我认为实际上值得让各州去这样做，你知道的，完成这些法律的实施工作并找出答案。

sentences.en: I just don't think that the harms are more likely to be on the side of not doing anything at all rather than trying to do a couple of, you know,
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，比起在各州尝试几种不同的创新策略来看看效果，什么都不做反而更有可能带来更大的危害。

sentences.en: different innovative strategies in different states to see.
sentences.zh: 通过在不同州尝试几种不同的创新策略来观察结果。

sentences.en: And then, you know, because there's been no federal law, there's obviously just this vacuum in the states and there's a lack of clarity.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，由于一直没有联邦法律，各州自然出现了这种真空状态，并且缺乏清晰度。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think there's been the D.C.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: conversation, the Trump administration conversation has been or discourse has really been, well, it's creating confusion.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府的对话或论调一直是，这会造成混乱。

sentences.en: And I think what's actually creating confusion is the lack of any kind of federal guidance.
sentences.zh: 而我认为真正造成混乱的是缺乏任何形式的联邦指导。

sentences.en: It's actually the states that are trying to sort of bring clarity to chaos.
sentences.zh: 实际上是各州在试图为混乱带来清晰度。

sentences.en: I mean, if if the states are the appropriate front line for figuring this stuff out,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果各州是弄清楚这些事情的合适最前线，

sentences.en: is the ideal form of that to eventually roll up into some kind of federal regulation that makes sense?
sentences.zh: 那么它的理想形式最终是否会演变成某种合理的联邦监管？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I think what the state patchwork does is test things out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为各州的拼凑立法起到了测试的作用。

sentences.en: Some things will work.
sentences.zh: 有些方法会奏效。

sentences.en: Some things will fail horribly.
sentences.zh: 有些方法会彻底失败。

sentences.en: I think it also creates some kind of the, you know, the so-called patchwork, I think, kind of creates some upward pressure.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也产生了一种，你知道的，所谓的拼凑立法，我认为它产生了一些向上的压力。

sentences.en: Because when, exactly to your point, Roman, when enough states act, federal policy or norms become, as the patchwork gets woven together, become kind of implicit.
sentences.zh: 因为当，完全如你所说，罗曼，当足够多的州采取行动时，随着拼凑立法交织在一起，联邦政策或规范就会变得隐性。

sentences.en: And I think it puts more pressure on it for the federal government to actually do something explicitly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这给联邦政府施加了更多压力，促使其真正采取显性行动。

sentences.en: I would also like if we widen the aperture just slightly broadly from like the AI companies that, you know, like that we're talking about now to social media,
sentences.zh: 我还希望，如果我们把视野稍微放宽一点，从我们现在讨论的人工智能公司扩大到社交媒体，

sentences.en: the social media example, which gives us another, you know, 15, 10 years more to think about.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体的例子，它为我们提供了另外10到15年的思考时间。

sentences.en: We've seen the utter failure, right, of the federal government to be able to legislate in that space.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了联邦政府在该领域进行立法遭遇的彻底失败，对吧？

sentences.en: And to the extent that we've got anything that looks like regulation or law or governance in that space, it's coming out of these lawsuits, like the lawsuits that we saw early,
sentences.zh: 就我们在该领域看到的任何类似于监管、法律或治理的东西而言，它们都来自于这些诉讼，比如我们早期看到的那些诉讼，

sentences.en: you know, that were decided a few weeks ago around, you know, Meta and YouTube.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，是几周前围绕Meta和YouTube做出裁决的诉讼。

sentences.en: And so I think there's also, I think if you are a state-level, you know, executive, if you're a governor or a state legislator,
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，如果你是一名州级行政长官，如果你是州长或州议员，

sentences.en: you're like thinking back about that example and just thinking, we can't wait and do this again.
sentences.zh: 你就会回想起那个例子，然后心想，我们不能再等下去重蹈覆辙了。

sentences.en: You know, the other, you know, as I said, the states are close to the harms they're hearing from constituencies.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，另一个，正如我所说，各州离危害很近，他们能听到选民的声音。

sentences.en: The way that we've been governing, if you think about the social media model, I mean, the young woman who was the plaintiff, and I think in the Meta case, she's 20 years old.
sentences.zh: 我们一直以来的治理方式，如果你想想社交媒体模式，我的意思是，那个作为原告的年轻女性，我想在Meta的案子里，她20岁。

sentences.en: I mean, this happened eight years ago or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这发生在八年前左右。

sentences.en: She was, you know, a child when this happened.
sentences.zh: 当这一切发生时，她还是个孩子。

sentences.en: And so the, you know, using liability and legal cases puts us quite far away from the harMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，利用责任追究和法律诉讼，使我们距离危害相当遥远。

sentences.en: And I think the states can be much closer.
sentences.zh: 而我认为各州可以距离得近得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, just to back up for a moment, by way of explanation, you're referring to the social media trials that are happening in California,
sentences.zh: 是的，为了稍微倒回补充一下，作为解释，你指的是正在加州发生的社交媒体诉讼，

sentences.en: where basically the state's attorney generals and private plaintiffs are suing, arguing that social media platforms are harmful products, which is,
sentences.zh: 基本上是各州的司法总检察长和原告在起诉，辩称社交媒体平台是有害产品，这在，

sentences.en: has a long storied history of legal liability in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在美国有着一段悠久而传奇的法律责任历史。

sentences.en: And actually, they're using the legal playbook of big tobacco.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们正在使用大型烟草公司的法律剧本。

sentences.en: You know, we kind of shut down big tobacco because we argued that the companies knew that these were harmful products and you sold them anyway.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们之所以能整顿大型烟草公司，是因为我们认为这些公司明知这些是有害产品，却还是将它们售出。

sentences.en: And that has proven so far to be successful in the social media space.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这在社交媒体领域迄今为止是成功的。

sentences.en: So I guess we could think of perhaps, you know, AI, some of these products are going to be dangerous and maybe we'll do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们可以认为，也许人工智能的一些产品会很危险，也许我们会采取这种做法。

sentences.en: Of course, I think you're right on her say that this is a backup, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为你说的对，这是一种后备方案，对吧？

sentences.en: We don't want to wait for the bad use case for people to be harmed.
sentences.zh: 我们不想等到出现糟糕的用例、人们受到伤害时才行动。

sentences.en: I mean, the nice thing about regulation is you can be proactive and say,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，监管的好处在于你可以采取前瞻性措施，并说：

sentences.en: we think this is going to happen or it is happening and we want to affect as many people as we can within the state or within the country.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这将会发生，或者它正在发生，我们希望在州内或国内尽可能多地影响人们。

sentences.en: My question is really more about what about the companies?
sentences.zh: 我的问题实际上更多是关于企业怎么办？

sentences.en: Not that I feel too bad for them, but if you're a company, it's pretty burdensome, I would think, that you've got to look at every state and see, like, what is every state doing?
sentences.zh: 倒不是说我多替它们感到难过，但如果你是一家公司，我想要应付每一个州并查看每个州在做什么，这会是相当繁重的负担。

sentences.en: So I would imagine that, you know, their first choice is no regulation, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，它们的第一选择是没有监管，对吧？

sentences.en: But their second choice must be federal regulation, no?
sentences.zh: 但它们的第二选择一定联邦监管，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I would disagree with that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，对此我有点不同看法。

sentences.en: I mean, let's have a friendly quibble about this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，让我们就此进行一场友好的辩论。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that the compliance burden argument, I think, is a bit overstated by companies, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为合规负担的论点被企业夸大了，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, that's just what companies do in their own interest in their lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这正是企业和它们的说客为了自身利益而做的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, and as I said, you know, I already mentioned, I think companies already in other policy spaces are navigating, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，正如我所说，我之前已经提到过，我认为企业在其他政策领域已经在应对，比如，

sentences.en: different consumer protection regimes for different states, different employment laws, different privacy frameworks.
sentences.zh: 针对不同州的的不同消费者保护制度、不同的就业法律、不同的隐私框架。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, the state of Illinois has this pretty strong biometric policy, you know, regime.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，伊利诺伊州就有相当严格的生物识别政策制度。

sentences.en: And yet, you know, companies were still, Clearview was still selling its facial recognition technology data set, for example.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道的，企业依然在这样做，例如Clearview仍然在出售其面部识别技术数据集。

sentences.en: So I think that the language from companies and lobbyists that say that state AI laws are, like, uniquely burdensome or especially burdensome,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为来自企业和说客的言论声称各州的人工智能法律，比如，具有独特或特别的负担，

sentences.en: I think doesn't really hold up when you think about these other examples of these other policy spaces.
sentences.zh: 当你考虑到其他政策领域的这些其他例子时，这种说法其实是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: The other thing I would say is that I think what your question, which is a common question, an important one, presumes, is that, like, if the states don't have a law,
sentences.zh: 我要说的另一件事是，你的问题（这是一个常见且重要的问题）所预设的是，如果各州没有法律，

sentences.en: there's no other governance or pressure being applied on the direction of AI governance.
sentences.zh: 就不会有其他治理或压力施加在人工智能治理的方向上。

sentences.en: Which certainly in the Trump administration is not true.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普政府执政期间，这显然是不可能的。

sentences.en: So, you know, so, okay, maybe you have to, you don't want to apply, you don't want to deal with California or Colorado,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，好吧，也许你必须这样做，你不想应付加利福尼亚州或科罗拉多州，

sentences.en: but you've got a Trump administration that's saying we're changing tariffs every day.
sentences.zh: 但你面对的是一个天天都在改变关税的特朗普政府。

sentences.en: You know, we've gone from Liberation Day to not Liberation Day back and forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们一直在“解放日”和“非解放日”之间反复横跳。

sentences.en: So companies are dealing with that, including AI companies.
sentences.zh: 因此，企业正在应对这些情况，包括人工智能公司在内。

sentences.en: You've got a Trump administration that is saying, we're uncertain about, we don't like immigration.
sentences.zh: 你面对的特朗普政府在说，我们对某些事情感到不确定，我们不喜欢移民。

sentences.en: We're uncomfortable with science and tech immigration.
sentences.zh: 我们对科学和技术移民感到不安。

sentences.en: If you want to bring a new technology talent AI company, you're going to have to pay $100,000 per visa if we allow you to have one to bring some, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你想引进一项新技术人才或人工智能公司，如果你想让我们允许你引进某位来自法国、韩国或类似地方的有才华的工程师，你将不得不为每张签证支付10万美元，

sentences.en: a talented engineer from France or, you know, Korea or something.
sentences.zh: 如果你想引进某位，你知道的，来自法国或韩国等地的杰出工程师的话。

sentences.en: And then they're also intervening in business.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还在干预商业活动。

sentences.en: So, you know, we've got the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们有美国，

sentences.en: taxpayer is a shareholder in NVIDIA or a shareholder in Intel.
sentences.zh: 美国纳税人成了英伟达的股东或英特尔的股东。

sentences.en: So the compliance burden question, I think,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为合规负担的问题，

sentences.en: is much too narrow given all of the different ways in which companies are being asked to respond to a kind of broad spectrum of AI governance.
sentences.zh: 鉴于企业被要求对广泛的人工智能治理做出反应的各种不同方式，显得过于狭隘了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And let's not forget, I should say, you know, the federal government and all of the state governments are huge customers.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，我应该说，你知道的，联邦政府和所有州政府都是大客户。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, customers can demand changes if they want.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，客户如果愿意，可以要求改变。

sentences.en: Procurement is an excellent vehicle.
sentences.zh: 政府采购是一个极好的手段。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Governor Newsom just signed this executive order that I think really leaned into that, including not only safety issues,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，纽森州长刚刚签署了这项行政命令，我认为它确实倾向于这一点，不仅包括安全问题，

sentences.en: but issues around discrimination and civil rights and liberties, which I thought was fantastic.
sentences.zh: 还包括有关歧视、公民权利和自由的问题，我认为这棒极了。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So we've talked a lot about sort of granular harms that are potentially happening or are happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了很多关于潜在发生或正在发生的具体危害。

sentences.en: But I do want to talk about your thoughts on what's on the horizon, the AI horizons.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想谈谈你对未来前景的看法，即人工智能的前景。

sentences.en: There seems to be this race to develop AGI or artificial general intelligence.
sentences.zh: 似乎存在着一场开发AGI（通用人工智能）的竞赛。

sentences.en: So the idea would be like not like, please find all the cats in this picture or write my high school essay on Pride and Prejudice.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法不是像，请在这张图片中找出所有的猫，或者帮我写一篇关于《傲慢与偏见》的高中论文。

sentences.en: It's like an all purpose, sophisticated AI with autonomy.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一个具备自主能力的万能、复杂的AI。

sentences.en: Now, you've spoken to a lot of people in tech.
sentences.zh: 现在，你和科技界的许多人谈过。

sentences.en: I've spoken to a few.
sentences.zh: 我也和一些人谈过。

sentences.en: It seems like some people in the AI policy world are extremely worried about this.
sentences.zh: 似乎人工智能政策界的一些人对此极为担忧。

sentences.en: Like we could create something that gets totally out of control, develops like a biological weapon, takes over our defense systeMs.
sentences.zh: 就像我们可能会创造出彻底失控的东西，开发出诸如生物武器之类的东西，接管我们的国防系统。

sentences.en: How concerned are you about this as a subject and then an object of regulation?
sentences.zh: 作为监管的一个主体和客体，你对此有多担忧？

sentences.en: So I'm concerned about it as I think some people are quite invested in the in the name and what the name means.
sentences.zh: 所以我对此感到担忧，因为我认为有些人非常执着于这个名字以及这个名字所代表的含义。

sentences.en: So people are quite invested in whether it's superintelligence or AGI.
sentences.zh: 所以人们非常纠结于它是超级智能还是AGI。

sentences.en: I'm not at all invested in the name and I don't really care.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不纠结这个名字，我根本不在乎。

sentences.en: So it keeps me out of some fights, but probably also keeps me out of some parties.
sentences.zh: 所以这既让我避免了一些争端，但也可能让我错过了不少派对。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But but I do but I do think that, you know, I prefer to use the phrase like advanced AI, like there are significant concerns about advanced AI.
sentences.zh: 不过，我确实认为，你知道的，我更倾向于使用“先进人工智能”这样的词，因为人们对先进人工智能存在重大的担忧。

sentences.en: So, example, if we think about the Doge early, you know,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果我们早些时候想想Doge，你知道的，

sentences.en: last year in the Trump administration and part of what the reporting and Wired and elsewhere was suggesting is that Doge was breaking the Privacy Act of 1974,
sentences.zh: 去年在特朗普政府期间，据《连线》杂志和其他地方的报道显示，Doge违反了1974年的《隐私法》，

sentences.en: which said that a lot of interagency organizations could not share data.
sentences.zh: 该法规定许多跨机构组织不得共享数据。

sentences.en: In part because you don't want the federal government to have administrative data about you from Health and Human Services, from Fannie Mae, from whatever,
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，你并不希望联邦政府掌握来自卫生与公众服务部、房利美以及其他任何机构的关于你的行政数据，

sentences.en: to be able to put into this kind of large surveillance kind of panopticon.
sentences.zh: 并把它们汇集进这种大规模的监控全景监狱中。

sentences.en: And I think what like powerful AI systems do is allow the interoperability of that data and the sort of discovery potential of associations that are dangerous,
sentences.zh: 我认为强大的AI系统所做的事情，恰恰是允许这些数据实现互操作，并有可能潜在地发现那些危险的关联，

sentences.en: things that we could never possibly know about ourselves or about others.
sentences.zh: 有些是我们绝不可能对自身或他人有任何了解的事情。

sentences.en: So that's like not even AGI, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这甚至还谈不上是通用人工智能（AGI），对吧？

sentences.en: Like, but that's just like sort of a powerful extreme.
sentences.zh: 这只是某种强大的极端情况。

sentences.en: So if you imagine a system having access to data about everyone in the United States, everyone in the world, being able to sort of constantly be evaluating that data,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想象一个系统能够访问美国乃至全世界每个人的数据，能够持续不断地评估这些数据，

sentences.en: running that data, and then making decisions.
sentences.zh: 处理这些数据，然后做出决策。

sentences.en: And again, you know, I mentioned at the beginning the various forms of the, you know, autonomy or not of different AI systems and to do it autonomously.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，正如我一开始提到的，各种不同AI系统在自主性方面的不同形式，即如何自主地运作。

sentences.en: So imagine not just all of the open claws, not all the little lobster claws of various agents, but like a really big claw,
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，不仅仅是所有的开放式机械爪，不仅仅是各种智能体的那些小龙虾爪，而是一个真正巨大的机械爪，

sentences.en: like a really powerful independent agent sort of acting in the world.
sentences.zh: 就像一个真正强大且独立的智能体在世界上行事。

sentences.en: And so we've got, you know, there's been some reporting and I've seen, you know, and some people, you know, discussing on social media things like, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们知道，有一些报道，我也看到过，而且有些人，你知道的，在社交媒体上讨论诸如这样的事情，

sentences.en: I use this agent and it wiped out my entire hard drive or it deleted all of my emails or that, right?
sentences.zh: 我用了这个智能体，然后它抹去了我的整个硬盘，或者它删除了我所有的电子邮件，诸如此类，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, and that's, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这确实发生了，

sentences.en: that's happening and we're not imagining an AI agent that was sentient and all-knowing and like decided that it was going to wipe out all of your email because you work too hard or because it doesn't want you to work or whatever.
sentences.zh: 而且我们并不是在想象一个具有感知能力、无所不知的AI智能体，它因为你工作太努力或者不想让你工作等原因，决定消灭你所有的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Those are just powerful systems that we're learning to use.
sentences.zh: 这些只是我们正在学习使用的强大系统。

sentences.en: So then you can imagine potentially a system having a bit more intentionality, a bit more sort of understanding of its stakes and being more powerful.
sentences.zh: 所以，你接下来可以想象，一个潜在的系统可能具有更多的意图性，对自身利害关系有更多的理解，并且变得更加强大。

sentences.en: The question then becomes, and I think this is where we trip ourselves up, well, how do you regulate that?
sentences.zh: 问题随之而来——我认为这也是我们常常陷入困境的地方——好吧，你该如何监管它？

sentences.en: It's just so powerful.
sentences.zh: 它实在是太强大了。

sentences.en: What are we going to do, you know?
sentences.zh: 我们能怎么办呢？

sentences.en: And before you get there, you need to imagine that companies can actually be told not to build a thing, you know?
sentences.zh: 而在你走到那一步之前，你需要想象一下，实际上是可以告诉公司不要去制造某个东西的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you can't tell them not to, or they can be told that they can't ship a thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不能告诉他们不准研发，或者可以告诉他们不能将其发布上市。

sentences.en: You can't tell a company what to create, but you can certainly say you can't ship this out into the world without certain controls.
sentences.zh: 你不能告诉一家公司应该创造什么，但你绝对可以对他们说，在没有特定控制措施之前，你不能把这东西推向世界。

sentences.en: Like someone needs to be able to have a kind of final decision on whether or not it ships or to be able to turn it off and on, or you can only run it for a few hours,
sentences.zh: 比如，需要有人对它是否发布拥有某种最终决定权，或者能够将其关闭和开启，或者你只能运行它几个小时，

sentences.en: or it can only have so much access to so much compute or so much data, you know?
sentences.zh: 或者它只能获得有限的计算资源或有限的数据访问权限，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And we're not having those kind of, I think, system-wide conversations.
sentences.zh: 而我认为，我们并没有在进行这种全系统范围的对话。

sentences.en: And, you know, to go back to where, you know, the kind of subject of the broader conversation, I mean, that is where you would want a smart, prudent,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，回到我们更广泛对话的主题上来，我的意思是，正是在这种情况下，你会希望有一个聪明、谨慎的

sentences.en: federal government to sort of weigh in, right?
sentences.zh: 联邦政府来介入表态，对吧？

sentences.en: That's where, you know, at that level of kind of nuance and both kind of level of abstraction and power, you might want there to be some sort of federal, I think,
sentences.zh: 正是在这种抽象程度与权力的细微差别层面，你可能会希望某种联邦层面的，我认为，

sentences.en: law or legislation or guidance.
sentences.zh: 法律、立法或指导方针能够发挥作用。

sentences.en: When we come back, Dr. Nelson explains her vision for finding a consensus on AI regulation, and whether she's optimistic the government will figure this out.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，纳尔逊博士将阐述她对寻找AI监管共识的愿景，以及她是否对政府能搞定此事保持乐观。

sentences.en: I mean, you developed this idea of a kind of thick alignment when it comes to AI governance.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在AI治理方面，你提出了“深度对齐”（thick alignment）这一理念。

sentences.en: Can you talk more about what thick alignment is and how that translates to regulation?
sentences.zh: 你能多谈谈什么是深度对齐以及它如何转化为监管吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's, you know, there's a wonderful writer, Brian Christian, who has a really, you know,
sentences.zh: 好的，这里有一位极好的作家布莱恩·克里斯蒂安（Brian Christian），他有一本非常重要的、

sentences.en: important book that I would commend to people called The Alignment Problem that is really writing about the first, the kind of early years of what we,
sentences.zh: 我向大家极力推荐的书叫做《对齐问题》（The Alignment Problem），书中真正记录了我们所经历的第一阶段、早期的一些年头，

sentences.en: what some people call AI safety, which is basically just like, how do we explain them?
sentences.zh: 也就是有些人所说的AI安全，这基本上就是指：我们该如何解释它们？

sentences.en: How do we interpret what they're doing?
sentences.zh: 我们如何解读它们在做什么？

sentences.en: How do we demonstrate that they're safe to the extent possible?
sentences.zh: 我们如何尽可能地证明它们是安全的？

sentences.en: And, you know, it was very much a kind of technical sense of thinking about alignment.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这在很大程度上是一种关于对齐的技术性思考方式。

sentences.en: So, you know, the system says that it's supposed to identify at 98 percent with a margin of error of two or three percent, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，该系统声称它能以98%的准确率识别这些人，误差范围为百分之二或百分之三，

sentences.en: these people in a facial recognition technology system.
sentences.zh: 这就是面部识别技术系统中的情况。

sentences.en: And for all intents and purposes, you would say that system is aligned, right?
sentences.zh: 出于所有的实际目的，你会说这个系统是对齐的，对吧？

sentences.en: But we know the system is misidentifying people.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，该系统正在错误识别人员。

sentences.en: We know in the Detroit metropolitan area that there have been more than half a dozen people misidentified by facial recognition technologies that someone somewhere in the development and deployment queue said this is aligned,
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在底特律都会区，有半打以上的人被面部识别技术错误识别，而开发和部署链条中的某个人在某个地方曾说过这是对齐的，

sentences.en: like this product works, right?
sentences.zh: 就像这个产品没问题一样，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, as we're thinking about AI systems and advanced AI systems, it's not just whether or not they kind of work technically.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考AI系统和先进AI系统时，这不仅关乎它们在技术上是否能行得通。

sentences.en: What happens when you or what can we anticipate or not anticipate when you deploy them?
sentences.zh: 当你部署它们时，会发生什么？或者我们能预见到什么、无法预见到什么？

sentences.en: And how do we create a process or an understanding that allows us to be thinking about alignment as something that needs to happen fairly continuously over time?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何建立一个流程或共识，让我们把“对齐”视为一件随着时间推移需要相当持续地进行的事情？

sentences.en: And also, that's something that needs to happen in conversation with the values of different communities and different societies.
sentences.zh: 并且，这也是一件需要与不同社群和不同社会的价值观进行对话来完成的事情。

sentences.en: So, alignment is not – so, by thick alignment, I am taking up the work of, you know, the philosopher Gilbert Ryle, but also the anthropologist Clifford Geertz,
sentences.zh: 因此，对齐不是——所以，谈到“深度对齐”，我借鉴了哲学家吉尔伯特·赖尔（Gilbert Ryle）以及人类学家克利福德·格尔茨（Clifford Geertz）的著作，

sentences.en: who was a professor here at the Institute of Advanced Study in Princeton, where I am,
sentences.zh: 他曾是我所在的普林斯顿高等研究院的教授，

sentences.en: who has this very famous sort of essay and the concept of thick description,
sentences.zh: 他有一篇非常著名的论文以及“深度描述”（thick description）的概念，

sentences.en: like that you don't really understand the world until you've really thought to understand contextually deeply what it means.
sentences.zh: 意思是，除非你真正深入地去理解其语境下的含义，否则你无法真正理解这个世界。

sentences.en: How do you describe it sort of deeply?
sentences.zh: 你如何去进行那种深度的描述？

sentences.en: And so, my provocation to AI safety researchers and my collaboration, actually, so it's not just a critical work, is sort of what does it mean to – like alignment is important.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对AI安全研究人员的诘问以及我的合作研究——实际上，这不仅是一项批判性工作——在于探讨这意味着什么——对齐很重要。

sentences.en: And safety, explainability, interpretability,
sentences.zh: 安全、可解释性、可诠释性，

sentences.en: all the things that you might put in that bucket are really important and are an important – and taken together are an important solution set for some of the harm mitigation that we might want to do in the space of AI.
sentences.zh: 所有你可能会归入这一类的事物都非常重要，并且综合起来，它们是我们在AI领域想要进行的一些危害缓解工作的重要解决方案集合。

sentences.en: But what does it mean to do that in a way that takes seriously the different contexts in which these tools might be used, the different values?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果想要以一种认真对待这些工具可能被使用的不同语境以及不同价值观的方式来做到这一点，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: So, if you think about, you know, Anthropic has created a constitution for AI, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想想，Anthropic公司为AI创建了一个宪法，举个例子。

sentences.en: Like, you know, who gets to weigh in on that?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁有权对此发表意见呢？

sentences.en: And are those the values that I want or others want?
sentences.zh: 这些是我想要的价值观，还是其他人想要的价值观？

sentences.en: You see this kind of value conversation coming up also, and even some of the Trump administration's kind of – the way that they frame sort of, quote-unquote,
sentences.zh: 你会发现这种关于价值观的对话也不断涌现，甚至在特朗普政府的一些表述中也能看到——他们构建所谓“引号内的”

sentences.en: ideological bias in AI.
sentences.zh: AI中的意识形态偏见的方式。

sentences.en: Like, who gets to decide what's biased in AI?
sentences.zh: 究竟谁有权决定什么是AI中的偏见？

sentences.en: There's a technical question about bias in AI, but who gets to decide sort of what is a biased chatbot?
sentences.zh: 关于AI中的偏见存在一个技术问题，但谁有权决定什么样的聊天机器人是有偏见的呢？

sentences.en: So, I think we just need to have a conversation we're not having about what it means to try to come to rough consensus values to the extent that's even possible, to try to have,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为我们只需要进行一场尚未开展的对话，讨论在甚至都未必可能的情况下，试图达成粗略共识的价值观意味着什么，

sentences.en: you know, high-level values to make decisions about these technologies.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，用高阶的价值观来对这些技术做出决策。

sentences.en: So, I think the AI Bill of Rights was one of the ways that we were trying to point to that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为《AI权利法案》（AI Bill of Rights）是我们试图指出这一点的方式之一。

sentences.en: But certainly, I think state laws are another way.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我认为各州的法律是另一种方式。

sentences.en: I mean, you have states sort of saying, I mean, that you might think of those as examples of thick alignment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，各州都在纷纷表态，你可以将这些视为深度对齐的例子。

sentences.en: Like, this is what our constituency cares about, and this is where we're going to lean in on in the regulatory space with regard to AI.
sentences.zh: 比如，这就是我们的选民所关心的，这也是我们在AI监管领域将重点发力的方向。

sentences.en: The other stuff, maybe we don't care about so much.
sentences.zh: 至于其他的东西，也许我们没那么关心。

sentences.en: But, like, I don't even know if I have thick alignment with President Trump as, like, a human.
sentences.zh: 但是，我甚至不知道我作为一个活生生的人，是否能和特朗普总统达成深度对齐。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, it seems harder and harder to have it, you know, like, when you're talking about all these hypothetical uses of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 当你谈到所有这些关于这东西的假想用途时，要做到这一点似乎越来越难了。

sentences.en: And, like, if something like a program is supposed to have inherent, you know, human values, a lot of those don't feel shared right now.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果像某个程序这样的东西本应具有内在的、你知道的人类价值观，那么其中许多价值观现在看来并不觉得是共享的。

sentences.en: No, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这很对。

sentences.en: I will say, you know, one of the things I've been doing since I left, so the AI Bill of Rights comes out in October of 2022.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，你知道，自我离开以来我一直在做的一件事是——《AI权利法案》于2022年10月发布。

sentences.en: And I've been since that time following its afterlives.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我一直在关注它的后续影响。

sentences.en: And some of its afterlives, I think, Roman, to your point, have been in red states.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，正如你所指出的，它的一些后续影响发生在红色州（共和党票仓）。

sentences.en: So there's been an Oklahoma AI Bill of Rights introduced as a bill.
sentences.zh: 因此，俄克拉荷马州曾提出过一项《俄克拉荷马州AI权利法案》作为议案。

sentences.en: You know, it didn't succeed ultimately, but it contained all of the five principles that we discussed previously,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它最终没有成功，但它包含了我们之前讨论过的所有五个原则，

sentences.en: plus a few more that were really good and actually quite stronger than some of the things that we suggested.
sentences.zh: 此外还有一些非常好的、实际上比我们建议的某些内容还要更强有力的原则。

sentences.en: More recently, in November, in Florida, Governor DeSantis introduced the Florida AI Bill of Rights,
sentences.zh: 最近在11月，在佛罗里达州，德桑蒂斯州长推出了《佛罗里达州AI权利法案》，

sentences.en: which contains within it all of the five principles that we have and lots of other things besides deep fakes, you know, child sexual abuse imagery,
sentences.zh: 其中包含了我们拥有的全部五个原则，以及除了深度伪造、儿童性虐待图像之外的许多其他内容，

sentences.en: a really nice clause that was around health insurance and not being able, you know, being able to get a decision around algorithmic uses of health insurance.
sentences.zh: 还有一个非常好的条款，围绕着健康保险，即不能——能够围绕健康保险的算法应用做出裁决。

sentences.en: So I totally take your point, Roman, but it's also clear that there are a few things that we agree are wrong or that we don't want that are like suboptimal for society.
sentences.zh: 所以我完全理解你的观点，罗曼，但也很显然，有一些事情是我们一致认为错误的不想要的，对社会而言是次优的。

sentences.en: And so I take, I think you're exactly right, but I also take some comfort in these Bill of Rights alignments that pop up here and there.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为你完全正确，但我也从这些不时涌现的权利法案对齐中感到了一些慰藉。

sentences.en: You sound optimistic about the future of AI regulation.
sentences.zh: 听起来你对AI监管的未来持乐观态度。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I'm not optimistic about, am I optimistic about regulation?
sentences.zh: 我对——我是对监管感到乐观吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, I think if we look at the history of technology policy at the federal level in the Congress, I mean, we, Elizabeth, correct me if I'm wrong, but I think, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们看看国会联邦层面的技术政策历史，我的意思是，伊丽莎白，如果我错了请纠正我，但我认为，你知道，

sentences.en: it's maybe not been since like the Communications Decency Act of 1996 that we've passed anything like a technology law.
sentences.zh: 自从1996年的《通信规范法》以来，我们可能就没有通过过任何类似的技术法律。

sentences.en: Like, you know, that's a long time.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: That's a generation.
sentences.zh: 那是一代人的时间。

sentences.en: So I'm not optimistic in that sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我从这个意义上讲并不乐观。

sentences.en: I think I'm optimistic with, you know, some people are calling it the tech backlash and I don't call it that, you know, I don't, I don't, I don't like that framing,
sentences.zh: 我认为我乐观的是，有些人称之为科技反弹，我不这么叫它，你知道，我不喜欢那种说法，

sentences.en: but there's a growing public empowerment to speak about what people want and don't want with regards to the way that AI systems are being developed and deployed.
sentences.zh: 但公众正在逐渐获得赋权，去表达人们对AI系统开发和部署方式的期望与反对。

sentences.en: So when I first started working, you know, and sort of big data and then, you know, as it became AI, you know, policy and research.
sentences.zh: 所以当我刚开始工作时，你知道，在搞大数据，然后，你知道，随着它变成AI政策和研究。

sentences.en: That's how you date yourself.
sentences.zh: 这就是你暴露年龄的方式。

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: You say big data in a room and people kind of like, cringe.
sentences.zh: 你在一个房间里说出“大数据”三个字，人们就会感到有些尴尬局促。

sentences.en: They're just like, oh, big data is so cringe.
sentences.zh: 他们就会觉得，噢，大数据太让人尴尬了。

sentences.en: So, you know, you would sit in rooms and say people can't possibly understand.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你以前坐在会议室里说人们根本不可能理解。

sentences.en: I mean, even now you hear people saying, you know, if folks don't have, you was here in D.C.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使现在你还能听到人们说，如果人们没有——你当时也在华盛顿，

sentences.en: actually when I was working in Washington.
sentences.zh: 实际上正是我在华盛顿工作的时候。

sentences.en: You know, if you don't really have a Ph.D., if you're a staffer on the Hill and you don't have a degree in machine learning or AI,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你真的没有博士学位，如果你是国会山的一名工作人员，并且没有机器学习或AI的学位，

sentences.en: like how could you possibly even begin to like offer guidance on how we should govern this technology?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么可能一开始就为我们该如何治理这项技术提供指导意见呢？

sentences.en: So, of course, you don't want people who know nothing about AI to be governing AI,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，你不会希望对AI一无所知的人来治理AI，

sentences.en: but I've been encouraged by the fact that the public has demonstrated that it is not true that you have to have a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 但我受到以下事实的鼓舞：公众已经证明，要想对AI治理领域发表一些见解，你并不非得拥有AI博士学位，这种说法是不成立的。

sentences.en: in AI to be able to say something about the AI governance space.
sentences.zh: 所以你在数据中心治理领域就能看到这一点。

sentences.en: So you see it in the space of governance of data centers.
sentences.zh: 因此人们确实，你知道的，那是一个AI治理和政策非常具体有形的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: So people have really, you know, that's a place where like AI governance and policy is quite tactile, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它非常贴近社区，关乎他们的水资源，关乎他们的能源消耗。

sentences.en: So it's quite, you know, it is in communities, it is about their water, it is about their energy use.
sentences.zh: 这就是AGI或超级智能真正落地生根的地方。

sentences.en: And it's where sort of AGI or super intelligence like lands on the ground.
sentences.zh: 这也是社区真正觉得他们对之拥有某种自主权的地方。

sentences.en: And it is where communities really feel they have a sense of agency around that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，我想我刚刚在新闻里看到缅因州已经禁止了数据中心一段时间。

sentences.en: So we're seeing, I think I just saw in the news that Maine has banned, you know, data centers for a time.
sentences.zh: 有很多宣布的大型项目都被搁置了，正在重新审视。

sentences.en: There's been, there were a lot of big projects announced that have been stalled, that are being revisited.
sentences.zh: 现在有报道称，许多社区中的这些数据中心协议是在保密协议（NDA）下与当地政客达成的，

sentences.en: There's reporting now about how a lot of these data center agreements in various communities were done with local politicians under NDAs,
sentences.zh: 以至于当地社区甚至无法了解其中一些协议的条款。

sentences.en: that local communities can't even know the terms of the agreement for some of these.
sentences.zh: 而人们正在对此进行强烈的抵制。

sentences.en: And people are really pushing back against that.
sentences.zh: 他们正在抵制对年轻人的伤害。

sentences.en: And they're pushing back against the harms to young people.
sentences.zh: 他们非常关注自杀意念以及聊天机器人如何助长这种意念。

sentences.en: They're very concerned about, you know, suicidal ideation and how chatbots encourage them.
sentences.zh: 所以我对法律感到乐观吗？

sentences.en: So am I optimistic about law?
sentences.zh: 绝对没有。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 但对于以下事实我感到乐观吗：你知道的，对于公司以及其他那些只想推动技术发展却不考虑危害和社会影响的精英们来说，

sentences.en: But am I optimistic about the fact that, you know, it's getting much more difficult for, you know, companies and, you know,
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点变得越来越困难了？

sentences.en: other elites who really want to just drive technology without thinking about the harms and the social implications to do that?
sentences.zh: 因为你有一大群声音在不断壮大，跨党派的，罗曼，他们说——也许谈不上对齐，但确实是跨党派的——他们说，我们不想要这个。

sentences.en: Because you've got a growing chorus of people, bipartisan, Roman, saying, maybe not aligned, but bipartisan, you know, saying that, like, we don't want this.
sentences.zh: 所以我找到了乐观，是的，受到了鼓舞。

sentences.en: And so I find optimism, no encouragement, yes.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一件事，我这里的一点看法是，令我感到滑稽的事情之一是，AI的最大支持者和广泛使用的推动者，

sentences.en: I think one of the things, my one point here is, like, one of the things that I think is funny is the biggest proponents of AI and the, you know,
sentences.zh: 某种程度上也是它最大的散布恐惧者。

sentences.en: broad use of it are kind of the biggest fear mongers of it, too.
sentences.zh: 就像，我认为他们某种程度上很享受那种“这超级强大”的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, I think they kind of enjoy the sort of sense of this is super powerful.
sentences.zh: 你们应该让我们做我们想做的事。

sentences.en: You should let us do what we want to.
sentences.zh: 它将在五年内毁灭人类。

sentences.en: And it's going to destroy humanity in five years.
sentences.zh: 就像，我认为他们两样都挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: Like, I think they like both of those things.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这两点都满足了他们的自负。

sentences.en: So I think both of them, like, feed into their ego.
sentences.zh: 它们都与权力有关。

sentences.en: They're both about power.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 最大的支持者竟然也是最大的恐惧制造者，这是一种奇怪的动态。

sentences.en: Are the biggest proponents is a weird dynamic.
sentences.zh: 这不像烟草监管，我们知道，那些想要监管的人只是站在防止危害的一边。

sentences.en: This is not like tobacco regulation where we, you know, where the people who wanted to, like, regulate were just on the side of harm.
sentences.zh: 而其他人则说没有危害。

sentences.en: And the other people were like, no harm.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的动态。

sentences.en: It's an odd dynamic.
sentences.zh: 这也是纠缠在所有这些事情中的其中一点，比如佛罗里达州的监管与加利福尼亚州的监管之间的对比。

sentences.en: And it's one of the things that's also, like, mixed up in all this stuff of, like, the Florida regulation versus the California regulation.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: The political valence of this stuff is much more complicated than most other things.
sentences.zh: 这些东西的政治倾向比大多数其他事物要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Yes, it's very complicated and kind of heterogeneous.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常复杂，而且有点多元杂合。

sentences.en: And so that's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很吸引人。

sentences.en: And I think there's some very interesting essays, articles, papers to be written about at a time of, you know, maybe historically,
sentences.zh: 我认为，在这样一个历史时期——你知道，

sentences.en: since we've been measuring highest polarization in American society, that you've got this growing negative sentiment about AI and that it's bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 自从我们开始衡量美国社会中最高的两极分化以来，你会发现公众对人工智能的负面情绪正在不断增加，而且这种情绪是跨党派的。

sentences.en: And that the issue set about which people are having agreement of their dissatisfaction around is growing, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，人们对之感到不满并达成共识的议题范围正在扩大，对吧？

sentences.en: So you go from kind of discrimination to young people and CSAM to fraud to, you know, health care.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种歧视，到针对年轻人和儿童性虐待材料（CSAM），再到欺诈，你知道，还有医疗健康。

sentences.en: Like, the space is just becoming much broader to data centers, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，这个领域正在变得更加广泛，例如还涉及到数据中心。

sentences.en: People obviously are worried about their jobs and worried about employment and what they're being told, Roman, to your point,
sentences.zh: 人们显然在担心自己的工作，担心就业情况，正如罗曼，正如你刚才提到的，

sentences.en: about powerful people saying our powerful tool is going to be really great and destroy everything, including all of your jobs, right?
sentences.zh: 那些有权有势的人在说，我们这门强大的工具将非常棒，同时又会摧毁一切，包括你们所有的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's, you know, it's a very interesting policy space.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，你知道，这是一个非常有趣的政策领域。

sentences.en: And it's a space, as I said, you know, I think of political encouragement, if not optimism.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这也是一个令人感到政治鼓舞——如果说不上是乐观的话——的领域。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, this seems like a new opportunity for a different kind of alignment, which is really kind of fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这似乎为某种不同形式的结盟提供了新的机遇，确实非常迷人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Dr. Nelson, I really appreciate you being here.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊博士，非常感谢您能来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's been great to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 和您交流非常愉快。

sentences.en: So that's the original seven articles of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这就是宪法最初的七条。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining for all of that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家一路以来的陪伴。

sentences.zh: 当然，还有需要探讨的修正案，总共有27条。
